title: How to Skip 2 Payments On Your Mortgage?
h2: A few things you should know
So, how does skip 2 payments on your mortgage work?
Is this a way to save money?
Transcript of the Mortgage Brothers Podcast

faqs.a: Yes, when refinancing, you typically skip 2 payments. There is no payment the month you close and no payment on the final month of the mortgage. For example, if you close on November 10th, you won’t make a December payment since mortgage payments are paid in arrears.

faqs.q: How does skipping 2 mortgage payments work?
faqs.a: When you close on your loan, the interest for that month is prepaid at closing. Since mortgage payments are paid in arrears, your next payment isn’t due until the following month. Essentially, the interest gets rolled into either the old loan or the new loan, but it’s not free—just shifted.

faqs.q: Does skipping mortgage payments save money?
faqs.a: No, skipping payments does not save money. It’s more like shifting payments. The total amount you owe remains the same—it just gets prepaid or delayed depending on the timing of your loan closing.
